text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak industrial production rose by 3.7 percent year-on-year in the first six months of this year to total 274.6 billion crowns.

- Brigita Schmoegnerova, an economic expert of the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL), said Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of EU enlargement will boost prices of potential foreign loans to Slovakia and will further discourage foreign companies from investing in the country.
- Opposition parties said they were planning a protest demonstration against the planned visit of French far-right National Front leader, Jean-Marie Le Pen, in Slovakia in September.
SME - The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, has rejected allegations that some its parliamentary deputies will quit the party.
- SDL has criticised the government for failing to present an analysis of reasons for exclusion of Slovakia from the first wave of candidates for EU membership.

- The opposition ethnic Hungarian Christian Democratic Movement (MKDH) said it would support attempts by other opposition parties to call an extraordinary session to demand the return of Jozef Gaulieder's mandate. Gaulieder was expelled from parliament last December.
PRAVDA - Hungary on Wednesday officialy confirmed that the Slovak and Hungarian Prime Ministers, Vladimir Meciar and Gyula Horn, will meet in Hungary on August 15.

- The state-owned Slovak Telecom company said the recent 10 percent increase in energy prices will boost its expenditures by some 20 million crowns, but added that it did not plan to increase prices of its services.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's engineering industry now accounts for about 14 percent of the country's entire industrial production. However, the engineering sector has been showing gradual production decline since the fall of communism in 1989.

- The number of employees in industry declined by 0.9 perecent year-on-year in the first six months of this year. The employment rate fell by 1.4 percent in the construction sector and by 0.3 percent in the trade sector.
